transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Leaking water onto the floor usually indicates a failed door seal, a cracked tub, or a loose hose connection. Since plug sockets are nearby, ensure the area is dry and power is off to prevent electrical hazards before investigating further. From what you have described, the most likely cause is sump seal / circulation-pump seal / drain-pump seal. Open the door and look all the way round the rubber seal on the tub edge, and along the bottom of the door, for splits, flattened sections or something caught on it. Is the seal damaged, was something caught on it (now removed), or does it look fine?

the seal looks fine i think. its still running tho and theres loads of bubbles coming out, housemate put fairy liquid in cos we ran out of tablets. water is going toward an extension lead on the floor, what do i do??

Move any water away from the extension lead and other electrical sources right now. From what you have described, the most likely cause is wrong detergent / washing-up liquid. Next: Stop or cancel the cycle immediately. Let me know what you find.
ok ive turned it off at the machine. theres still water on the floor spreading toward the lead tho, what do i do now??

Do not touch the machine or the wet area until it is safe. From what you have described, the most likely cause is is there water in the base, and where is it leaking from (find the source first). Can you tell me whether the drain pump keeps running with an empty tub?
idk how to tell if the pump is running, ive turned it off. the water is still going toward the extension lead tho, should i unplug it or what??

Do not touch the plug with wet hands and ensure no one stands in the water while doing so. Tall trays or items hanging below the lower rack can deflect the spray straight at the door seal. With the racks loaded, turn each spray arm by hand. Was anything catching the arms or pointing at the door (and have you moved it), or is everything clear?
idk about the spray arms, i havent touched anything. can you just tell me if its safe to unplug it or should i turn the power off at the fuse box?? the water is nearly at the lead

It is safer to switch the power off at the main fuse box because water is near an extension lead, creating a high risk of electric shock. Do not attempt to unplug the machine while standing in water or touching wet surfaces. Check where the inlet hose connects at the tap under the sink and at the dishwasher end for drips, a loose fitting or a split. Was a connection loose (and is it tight now), is the hose damaged, or is it dry?
ok ill go to the fuse box now. the hose under the sink i havent checked, i dont want to go near the water. is it ok to just leave it once the power is off?

No, you should not just leave it because there is still a significant risk of electrical shock from the water reaching the extension lead. You need to switch off the main fuse box immediately and then address the standing water to prevent damage or injury. Check the drain hose along its length and where it joins the sink waste for drips, a loose clip or a split. Was it loose (and is it refitted now), is the hose split, or is it dry?
i dont know, i havent looked at the drain hose and im not going near the water. im at the fuse box now, is it ok to switch it all off?

Yes, switching off the power at the main fuse box is the correct and safe action. This stops the leak and prevents electricity from reaching the water near your extension lead. Does it stay dry, or does it still leak?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
ok ive switched it all off at the fuse box. the water on the floor is still there but i cant tell if its still leaking, im not going near it. what do i do now?

Turn off the main power supply immediately to prevent electric shock, as water is near an extension lead. Do not touch any electrical sockets or the appliance until the area is completely dry and safe. Next: Establish whether there is water in the base tray and where it is coming from. Let me know what you find.
